posts.label: Meme 1
posts.overlay_text: when he drops a red flag and your whole journal from January warned you about this
posts.ig_caption:
Your journal was right 👀

Tonight's prompt: what's a pattern you recognized in someone, explained away, and watched repeat anyway?
posts.fb_caption: Okay but why does journaling literally give you receipts on yourself? 😅 Tonight's prompt: what's a pattern you recognized in someone, explained away, and watched repeat anyway? Drop a word in the comments — I'll start: *waiting*.
posts.hypothesis: Pairing the wry-grimace clip with the 'Dating in 2026 red flags' meme format because this trend is at peak virality in Aug 2026 and recognition posts drive comment threads; expecting above-median comments as readers share their own journaling receipts.

posts.label: Meme 2
posts.overlay_text: me rereading every journal entry from this summer at once
posts.ig_caption:
End of August hitting different when you wrote it all down 📖✨

Tonight's prompt: what did this summer teach you about yourself that you're carrying into the rest of the year?
posts.fb_caption: There is something so quietly devastating about reading back what you wrote in June. 🍂 Tonight's prompt: what did this summer teach you about yourself that you're carrying into the rest of the year? Save this one — it's a good one to come back to in December.
posts.hypothesis: Riding Noah Kahan's 'End of August' audio wave with the ugly-cry clip because rereading summer entries is a universal journaling moment; end-of-season reflection posts historically over-index on saves in this niche, and saves are IG's key algorithm signal.

posts.label: Quote 1
posts.quote: You must do the thing you think you cannot do.
posts.fb_caption: The journal entry you keep skipping? That's the one. ✨ Tonight's prompt: what's one thing you've been writing around instead of through — and what would it take to face it on the page? Save this one and come back to it. 💜
posts.hypothesis: Short Eleanor Roosevelt directive paired with a resistance-to-reflection prompt, testing whether a challenge-framed quote earns more FB comments than the comfort-themed quotes we've been running — prediction is more comments, fewer saves.

posts.label: Quote 2
posts.quote: My mission in life is not merely to survive, but to thrive.
posts.fb_caption: End of summer is a good time to ask the real question. 🌿 Tonight's prompt: in what area of your life are you surviving right now when you know you're meant to be thriving? Write the honest answer. Zenie holds it safe.
posts.hypothesis: Maya Angelou's thrive line with an end-of-summer 'surviving vs thriving' prompt; this register of honest self-inventory has historically driven the most FB comments of any quote format we've run, and September feels like the right moment to ask it.
